extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents/applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for handling, entering, refusing, and documenting amendments filed after notice of allowance under 37 CFR 1.312, and related rules on affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 (swearing back). Aimed at guiding examiners and advising applicants on what amendments will be entered and under what conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition/examples of 'amendment' under 37 CFR 1.312
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment of an application by applicant after allowance falls within the guidelines of 37 CFR 1.312. Examples of 'amendments' by applicant after allowance which must comply with 37 CFR 1.312 include: (A) an amendment to the specification, (B) a change in the drawings, (C) an amendment to the claims, (D) a change in the inventorship, (E) the submission of prior art, (F) a petition to correct the spelling of an inventor’s name, (G) a petition to change the order of the names of the inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any change in the file record broadly encompasses an 'amendment' and thus is subject to 37 CFR 1.312 and the related processing requirements (e.g., compliance with 37 CFR 1.121).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: amendment must be filed before issue fee paid
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 must be filed on or before the date the issue fee is paid, except where the amendment is required by the Office of Patent Publication (PUBS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed after payment of the issue fee, 37 CFR 1.312 no longer permits filing the amendment unless PUBS waives the rule (see PUBS-required amendments). Use form PTOL-90/PTOL-90C for notices. If amendment filed after issue fee, it will not be entered (see form paragraph 13.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 required
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 must comply with the provisions of 37 CFR 1.121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the amendment is non-compliant under 1.121 and entry would otherwise be recommended, the examiner may enter the amendment and correct non-compliance using an examiner's amendment (e.g., incorrect status identifier). If non-compliant and not entered, attach a Notice of Non‑Compliant Amendment. See MPEP § 714 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of supplemental oaths/declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: With the exception of a supplemental oath or declaration submitted in a reissue, a supplemental oath or declaration is not treated as an amendment under 37 CFR 1.312. A supplemental reissue oath or declaration is treated as an amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 because the correction of the patent which it provides is an amendment of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a reissue oath or declaration submitted after allowance to be entered, the reissue applicant must comply with 37 CFR 1.312 in the manner set forth in the section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-Notice-of-Allowance examiner authority (formal corrections)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the Notice of Allowance has been mailed the application is technically no longer under the jurisdiction of the primary examiner. The primary examiner can, however, make examiner's amendments and has authority to enter amendments submitted after Notice of Allowance which embody merely the correction of formal matters in the specification or drawing, or formal matters in a claim without changing the scope thereof, or the cancellation of claims from the application, without forwarding to the supervisory patent examiner for approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal matters may be entered by the primary examiner without supervisory approval. If the amendment affects disclosure or claim scope, supervisory approval is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervisory approval required for non-formal amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments other than those which merely embody the correction of formal matters without changing the scope of the claims require approval by the supervisory patent examiner. The Technology Center Director establishes TC policy with respect to trivial informalities and whether they may be treated without supervisory review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The TC policy balances (A) adequate clarity of disclosure and (B) sufficient claim definition for an enforceable contract when deciding treatment of trivial informalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration is discretionary; not a matter of right
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of an amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 cannot be demanded as a matter of right. Prosecution should be complete at time of Notice of Allowance. Amendments may be considered where they (A) are shown to be needed for proper disclosure or protection of the invention, and (B) require no substantial amount of additional work by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if an amendment could improve the record, entry is discretionary and should be weighed against the Office workload and the nature of the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required remarks when amendment affects disclosure/scope/adds claim
rubrics_metrics.description: For amendments affecting the disclosure, the scope of any claim, or that add a claim, the remarks accompanying the amendment must fully and clearly state the reasons on which reliance is placed to show: (A) why the amendment is needed; (B) why the proposed amended or new claims require no additional search or examination; (C) why the claims are patentable; and (D) why they were not presented earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirements of 37 CFR 1.111(c) with respect to pointing out the patentable novelty of any claim sought to be added or amended apply in the case of an amendment under 37 CFR 1.312.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not to be used for continued prosecution; acceptable bases for non-entry
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.312 was never intended to provide a way for the continued prosecution of an application after it has been passed for issue. When the recommendation is against entry, a detailed statement of reasons is not necessary; the simple statement that the proposed claim is not obviously allowable and briefly the reason why is usually adequate. Sufficient reasons include: (A) an additional search is required; (B) more than a cursory review of the record is necessary; or (C) the amendment would involve materially added work on the part of the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may use these concise reasons when recommending non-entry. Dependent-claim additions may be less likely to be refused, but new matter, sufficiency of disclosure, or undue multiplicity issues can still apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments filed with motions under 37 CFR 41.208
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment filed with a motion under 37 CFR 41.208(c)(2) applies to an application in issue, the amendment is not entered unless and until the motion has been granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not enter amendments tied to a motion until the Board or deciding authority grants the motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional fees required for added claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If the amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 adds claims (total and independent) in excess of the number previously paid for, additional fees are required. The amendment is not considered by the examiner unless accompanied by the full fee required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 607 and 35 U.S.C. 41 for specifics on claim fees; do not process additions without full payment or authorization to charge account/credit card.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing/routing and prompt examiner consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments under 37 CFR 1.312 that affect disclosure, add claims, or change claim scope are sent by OIPE to the Publishing Division and forwarded to the Technology Center that allowed the application (or scanned in IFW and messaged to PUBS and the TC). The amendment is promptly considered by the examiner who indicates 'Enter — 312', 'Do Not Enter' or 'Enter In Part' in red ink on the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hand-delivered amendments are no longer accepted in the TC (unless PUBS specifically requires). For IFW, print the first page and annotate before scanning. Prompt consideration and correct routing are required to resume issue processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality of entry and required signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: If the amendment is favorably considered, it is entered and a Response to Rule 312 Communication (PTO-271) is prepared. The primary examiner indicates recommendation by stamping and signing; entry that affects scope of claims requires the signature of the supervisory patent examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.85 for entry and 7.87 for non-entry. The technical support staff mailing the PTO-271 does not officialize admission until supervisory approval where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry in part—procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment containing plural claims/amendments includes some acceptable and some not, the acceptable claims or amendments should be entered if the application is a paper file. Refused claims or amendments should be canceled in pencil on the amendment. Examiner should submit PTO-271 recommending entry of acceptable portion and nonentry of remaining portion with reasons; indicate entered claims by number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims may need renumbering to run consecutively. For IFW processing follow IFW Manual. Entry in part is not recommended unless full additional fee accompanies the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment filed after period for reply expired
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is not prosecuted within the period set for reply and thereafter an amendment is filed without a petition for extension of time and fee under 37 CFR 1.136(a), such amendment shall be placed in the file of the application, but not formally entered. Technical support staff must immediately notify applicant that the amendment was not filed within time and the application is abandoned unless a petition and fee are timely filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 711.02 and § 710.02(e). Technical support staff should process these notifications promptly and applications of this type are handled specially to ensure applicant awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office vs Technology Center vs IFW stamping and date handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments in paper files are stamped with the date of receipt in the Technology Center ('Technology Center Date' stamp) and the date of receipt by the Office ('Office Date' stamp). The Office Date should be referred to in writing to the applicant with regard to the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All amendments received in technical support are processed and delivered to supervisory patent examiner for review and distribution. Amendments replying to a final action should be screened and processed within 24 hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who evaluates compliance with 37 CFR 1.121
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the amendment after final rejection for compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 should be left to the examiner, and not treated by the technical support staff before forwarding the amendment to the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner determines the proposed amendment is not in compliance, the examiner should notify applicant and attach a Notice of Non‑Compliant Amendment to the advisory action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadvertently entered amendments have no legal effect
rubrics_metrics.description: If the technical support staff inadvertently enters an amendment when it should not have been entered, such entry is of no legal effect, and the same action is taken as if the changes had not been actually made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unauthorized entry should be deleted or noted as 'Not Officially Entered' on the amendatory paper. If paper is retained but not entered, give it a paper number and list on the file wrapper with the notation 'Not Entered.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Discourtesy/delinquent behavior: 37 CFR 1.3
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and their attorneys or agents are required to conduct their business with the USPTO with decorum and courtesy. Papers presented in violation of this requirement will be submitted to the Director and will not be entered; a notice of the non-entry of the paper will be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical support staff should briefly review papers before entry to determine discourteous remarks. If discourteous, either ignore the discourtesy or submit the paper to the TC Director for review. Complaints against examiners/employees must be made in separate correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of amendments ordinarily denied entry — A: unpatentable claim/new search when prosecution closed
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment presenting an unpatentable claim, or a claim requiring a new search or otherwise raising a new issue in an application whose prosecution before the primary examiner has been closed (e.g., all claims allowed; all claims finally rejected; some claims allowed and remainder finally rejected).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such amendments ordinarily are denied entry, though a subsequent showing by applicant may lead to entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of amendments ordinarily denied entry — B: substitute specification not complying with 37 CFR 1.125
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute specification that does not comply with 37 CFR 1.125 is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 608.01(q) and § 714.20 for substitute specification submission rules. A proper substitute specification will normally be accepted if compliant, but entry after notice of allowance is not a matter of right.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of amendments ordinarily denied entry — C: examiner-suggested claim not timely presented
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent claim suggested by the examiner and not presented within the time limit set or an extension thereof, unless entry is authorized by the Director, is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP Chapter 2300 for conditions where Director may authorize entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of amendments ordinarily denied entry — D: copied patent claims (conditional)
rubrics_metrics.description: While copied patent claims are generally admitted even though the application is under final rejection or on appeal, under certain conditions the claims may be refused entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP Chapter 2300 and § 714.19 for procedure when amendment includes claims copied from a patent. Entry of copied claims is not a matter of right.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of amendments ordinarily denied entry — E: unsigned/improperly signed papers
rubrics_metrics.description: An unsigned or improperly signed amendment or one signed by a suspended or excluded attorney or agent is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify signatures and authority before entry; lack of proper signature is a ground for non-entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of amendments ordinarily denied entry — F: filed after expiration of statutory reply period
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed in the USPTO after the expiration of the statutory period or set time period for reply and any extension thereof is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such late-filed amendments should be placed in the file but not formally entered unless proper petition/fee are filed; applicant must be notified immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of amendments ordinarily denied entry — G: cannot be entered with accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment so worded that it cannot be entered with certain accuracy is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity and ability to accurately enter changes (e.g., ambiguous redrafting) is essential; ambiguous wording should be refused entry until clarified.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of amendments ordinarily denied entry — H: canceling all claims with no substitute
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment canceling all of the claims and presenting no substitute claim or claims is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.115(b)(1) and MPEP § 711.01 and § 714.01(e) for nonresponsive amendments and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of amendments ordinarily denied entry — I: application no longer within examiner's jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment in an application no longer within the examiner’s jurisdiction is ordinarily denied entry, with certain exceptions in applications in issue and except on approval of the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714.16 regarding amendments in applications in issue and Director approval requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of amendments ordinarily denied entry — J: drawings alleged to contain new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the drawing held by the examiner to contain new matter are not entered until the question of new matter is settled. This practice of nonentry because of alleged new matter does not apply to amendments to the specification and claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolve new matter questions before entry of drawing amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of amendments ordinarily denied entry — K: objectionable remarks (37 CFR 1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendatory paper containing objectionable remarks that, in the opinion of the examiner, brings it within the condemnation of 37 CFR 1.3, will be submitted to the TC Director and may be refused entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the TC Director finds violation of 37 CFR 1.3, a notice of non-entry will be sent to applicant. See MPEP § 714.25 and § 1003.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of amendments ordinarily denied entry — L: non‑permanent ink/easily erasable paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments not in permanent ink or on 'easily erasable paper' are ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure amendments are on appropriate paper and in permanent ink per MPEP § 714.07.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of amendments ordinarily denied entry — M: excess claims without fee
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment presenting claims (total and independent) in excess of the number previously paid for and not accompanied by the full fee for the claims or an authorization to charge a deposit account or credit card is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 509 and § 607 for fee procedures; require payment or authorization before entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of amendments ordinarily denied entry — N: canceling elected invention claims and only presenting nonelected invention claims
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment canceling all claims drawn to the elected invention and presenting only claims drawn to the nonelected invention should not be entered as it is nonresponsive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should be notified per MPEP § 714.03 and § 714.05. See MPEP § 821.03 for election rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of amendments ordinarily denied entry — O: noncompliance with 37 CFR 1.121 (e.g., missing replacement paragraphs/claim listings)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment including changes to the specification/claims which is not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121, e.g., one which does not include replacement paragraphs or claim listings, is ordinarily denied entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714 for treatment of amendments not in compliance with 1.121; require properly formatted replacement text or claim listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of amendments ordinarily denied entry — P: preliminary amendment interfering with first Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment that unduly interferes with the preparation of a first Office action may be denied entry; factors are set forth in 37 CFR 1.115(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider 37 CFR 1.115(b) factors and MPEP § 714.01(e) when deciding whether to enter preliminary amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of amendments ordinarily denied entry — Q: supplemental reply not during suspension period
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental reply is not entered as a matter of right unless it is filed during a suspension period under 37 CFR 1.103(a) or (c). See 37 CFR 1.111(a)(2) and MPEP § 714.03(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental replies outside suspension periods should not be entered unless special circumstances apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments entered in part — examples and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid confusion an amendment generally should not be entered in part; where strict observance would do more harm than good, acceptable portions should be entered and unacceptable ones denied entry. Examples: (A) unacceptable substitute specification with acceptable amendatory matter — enter in part; (B) amendment under 1.312 partly approved and partly disapproved — enter only approved part; (C) in Quayle action where formal defects cured but new claims unpatentable/would require search — enter only formal matter; (D) amendment accompanying a motion granted only in part — enter to extent motion granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate entered portions with 'Enter' in red ink and initials. For IFW processing follow IFW Manual. Entry in part typically requires accompanying fees for any added claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Swearing back under 37 CFR 1.131 — general rule and required showing
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.131 allows an affidavit or declaration to establish invention of the subject matter of a rejected claim prior to the effective date of the reference; the showing must establish reduction to practice prior to the effective date of the reference, or conception prior to that date coupled with due diligence to reduction to practice or to filing. Original exhibits of drawings or records, or photocopies thereof, must accompany and form part of the affidavit or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.131(a) was amended to reflect NAFTA, URAA/WTO, and other laws; effective dates for proving inventive activity in foreign countries depend on treaty/entry dates. The affidavit overcomes the rejection, not the reference itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where 37 CFR 1.131 affidavits/declarations can be used — antedating 102(a) or 102(e) references
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 may be used (A) to antedate a reference or activity that qualifies as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) and not under 102(b) (e.g., reference date less than 1 year prior to applicant's effective filing date); (B) to antedate a reference that qualifies as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e), where the reference shows but does not claim the same patentable invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the 102(a) reference is a U.S. patent or patent application publication that claims the same patentable invention, it may not be antedated. See MPEP § 715.05 and § 706.02(a), § 2136–§ 2136.03 for what qualifies as prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations where 37 CFR 1.131 is inappropriate (statutory bars, same invention, admissions, 102(f), etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 is not appropriate in the following situations: (A) reference publication date more than 1 year prior to applicant's effective filing date (statutory bar under 35 U.S.C.102(b)); (B) reference U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication claims the same patentable invention; (C) reference is a foreign patent for the same invention to applicant issued prior to the domestic filing date where an earlier foreign filing was made more than 12 months earlier (35 U.S.C.102(d)); (D) where applicant's parent application's effective filing date or PCT proved filing date is prior to the effective date of the reference (unnecessary); (E) reference is a prior U.S. patent to the same entity claiming the same invention (double patenting); (F) reference is disclosure of a prior U.S. patent to the same party not copending (dedication issues); (G) applicant clearly admitted on the record that subject matter is prior art; and (H) subject matter relied upon is prior art under 35 U.S.C.102(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite the pertinent case law (e.g., In re Hellsund, In re Garfinkel, In re Blout, In re Lopresti) and MPEP references when evaluating appropriateness of a 1.131 affidavit.
